data.text: Mei argued the pilots covered no hospitals, transport operators or care homes, and fewer than half the firms measured output consistently, so the gains were partly redistributed rather than created.
Mei cited nine shift-based organisations holding coverage constant that needed 18% to 27% more staffed hours on a shorter week; two clawed part back within six months, seven did not measure it.
Mei conceded the status-quo-is-also-a-policy line lands and that doing nothing costs money in absence, agency fees and resignations.
Mei closed urging sequence, explicit exemption of continuous services, and mandated measurement before a nationwide default, calling Amara's ward result good but untested for round-the-clock cover.
